title: Mandala Goal Setting Method
summary: The creator explains the Mandala goal-setting method, which breaks down any major goal into a structured 9x9 grid of actionable steps. By decomposing goals and focusing on high-leverage actions, individuals can systematically achieve what they set out to do.
key_points: Write your main goal in the center box of a 3x3 grid.
Brainstorm and fill the 8 surrounding boxes with the requisite steps or components needed to achieve the main goal.
Expand the grid into a 9x9 mandala by surrounding the main 3x3 grid with eight more 3x3 grids, putting each of the 8 sub-goals in the center of their respective grids.
Populate the external 3x3 grids with 8 actionable habits or steps required for each sub-goal, resulting in 64 total actions.
Select high-leverage items (ideally 1 to 5-8 items per outer box) that you can control and that make a meaningful difference.
Ensure your actions are distinct and controllable rather than vague or dependent on external factors.
Iterate and focus on 5-8 items for the first week, then add another set of 5-8 items in subsequent weeks over 8 to 12 weeks.
